_note: TEACHES THE ECONOMY. Won by owning a house AND fifteen villagers.
TWO WIN ROWS, AND THEY ARE ANDed. 'A house and fifteen villagers' is one objective in
two halves, which is exactly what multiple `win` rows mean (PLAN.md 11.8). An OR would
need grouping and no scenario wants one yet.
THE OBJECTIVE AND THE MESSAGE ARE THE OWNER'S OWN WORDS, 2026-09-02, and the target
moved from 10 villagers to 15 with them. 15 is a better number than it looks: MapGen
gives every player a town centre worth 10 population and 5 villagers, and a house is
worth 5, so 15 villagers is reachable with EXACTLY ONE HOUSE and not reachable without
one. That makes the two win rows depend on each other instead of merely sitting beside
each other -- the player cannot satisfy the villager half while ignoring the build half.
(A target of 5 would be a scenario already won on tick 0 and would teach nothing; the
lesson is that villagers make villagers, and that population needs housing.)
THE OPPONENT IS PASSIVE, which runs its whole economy and never attacks -- so this
scenario cannot be lost by being raided while you learn. Elimination is still the loss
(you own nothing, you are out), because that is true on every map in this game whatever
a file declares, which is why no lose condition is written here.
SCENARIO MODE MUST NOT LET CONQUEST WIN THIS, and as of 15.2 it does not: killing the
passive AI's five villagers and its town centre eliminates THEM and ends nothing, so
this cannot be won with two villagers and no house. WinConditionSystem._scenario is
where that fork lives -- conquest's loss without conquest's win.
A FOUNDATION IS NOT A HOUSE. ObjectiveSystem counts COMPLETE buildings only, which is
the population cap's rule and deliberately not the elimination rule's, so pegging out a
house and walking away does not tick this row.
name: How To Gather and Build
description: Villagers gather food, wood, gold and stone, and they build. Put up a house and grow to fifteen villagers.
message:
Objective: Build 1 house, and reach 15 Villagers.

Overview: Select a single villager and tap the build icon on the bottom left hand of the screen, tap the House tile, then drag the house to an open spot on the map where it turns GREEN and place it.

Select some villagers and tap on a berry bush -- look for an ORANGE tile flash to indicate they will gather it.

Train more villagers from your town centre. One house is exactly enough population for fifteen.
_note_map: THE MAP IS THE SAVED map.png BESIDE THIS FILE (2.4c, PLAN.md 11.3). `seed` below is
PROVENANCE ONLY -- it records how the map was first generated and nothing reads it to
rebuild one. build_config() does not call MapGenerator at all, which is the owner's
ruling of 2026-09-01: generating is a one-off authoring step, not something a launch
does. That closed the 'a pinned seed is not a pinned map' defect for good, since
FastNoiseLite's float maths is not identical between an ARM phone and an x86 desktop.
